recipes.name: Pumpkin Pie without Evaporated Milk
ingredients_raw: 2 cups white sugar, or more to taste
2 teaspoons ground cinnamon, or more to taste
0.5 teaspoon ground nutmeg, or more to taste
0.25 teaspoon ground cloves, or more to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 475 degrees F (245 degrees C).
Combine pumpkin purée, milk, sugar, eggs, flour, cinnamon, nutmeg, salt, and cloves in a large bowl; mix with an electric mixer until smooth. Pour evenly into pie shells.

Bake in the preheated oven for 10 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) and continue to bake until filling is set, 35 to 45 more minutes. Place pies on a wire rack to cool. Serve warm or at room temperature.

raw_recipe.headline: Pumpkin Pie without Evaporated Milk
raw_recipe.description: For this delicious pumpkin pie, whole milk is stirred into pumpkin purée, so it's a bit lighter than others but still just as delicious and creamy.

review.reviewBody:
This recipe is wonderful! I choose it because of being able to use regular milk instead of evaporated which I did not have.
I have now made this about 5 times and sometimes I use mashed cooked sweet potato or mashed cooked butternut squash instead of the pumpkin. Both options turn out great!

I used pumpkin pie spice instead of the individual spices but still kept the cinnamon and backed off just a bit on the sugar per other reviews. I used a whisk instead of a hand mixer. Anyone who doesn’t read the recipe and thinks it’s only for one shell is mistaken, it clearly says 2 shells. Great recipe.

A great option for people with dairy issues: I swapped out the milk for unsweetened coconut milk (NOT to be confused with coconut cream) and there is NO coconut taste, and the texture and flavor are IDENTICAL to traditional pumpkin pie. I recommend using Aroy-D brand coconut milk, but Native Forest brand is good too. Using coconut milk, it took about 55 minutes to bake with a pre-heated oven. Also, make sure to reduce the sugar to 1 cup or less like other people have said and it will turn out great! I also swapped out the suggested spices for the ones in the Libby's brand pie recipe; for 2 pies use 2 teaspoons cinnamon, 1 teaspoon ground ginger, and 1/2 teaspoon of ground cloves. Note: Make sure to get a good quality of coconut milk which has a thicker cream-like texture, than some of the cheap watery ones for best results. Enjoy!

This would be a five star, except for the unreasonable amount of sugar called for in the recipe. I made 1 1/2 batches, which made 3 pies, and I only put in ONE CUP TOTAL! It was plenty sweet enough. I used raw sugar. I also cooked my own pumpkin, and drained it using a square of old sheet fabric in a colander, and then squeezing until it was reduced to the thickness of canned pumpkin (the volume left was less than 1/2 of what I started with). The filling still seemed a bit runny to me, (because of using my pumpkin, not because of the recipe) so I added a heaping Tablespoon of cornstarch. The pies turned out perfectly!

super with amendments - 1 c sugar maybe 1-1/2, cook more like 45 extra minutes, and it may be more than fits in a 9 or even 10 inch shell - I also added a little ginger - great texture - also I serve COLD
This was a good pumpkin pie but too sweet. Next time I will use extra pumpkin pie spice and 1 3/4 cup sugar to cut back on sweetness.

It was really good and easy to make. I used a little pumpkin that I had and it wasn't enough for 2 cups so I added some sweet potato to it. I also had about 4 oz cream cheese left from Thanksgiving so I thought id fold it in with the ingredients so it didn't go to waste. I used pumpkin pie spice too. It turned out really rich and creamy. Just perfect with some Cool Whip.
Reduce sugar to one cup and double the spices. Perfect!
I used the Shortbread crust on this site (did not pre-bake crust), everything turned out quite well. I also cut way back on sugar - only used one cup.
The only thing i did was reduce the sugar by 1 cup, otherwise this recipe was a big hit at home. I'll be making this again.

I was surprised by how nicely this turned out without using evaporated milk or sweetened condensed milk. I baked a fresh pumpkin in the oven first, and that truly gives it the richest flavor since the sugars carmelize so nicely that way. I reduced the milk to 1.5 cups, added 2 extra tablespoons of flour and reduced the sugar to 1 cup. That actually was PLENTY of sugar, so don't overdo it. I will make this one again and again.
My mom and grandma both said it was the best pumpkin pie they have ever eaten. It was also super easy to follow the recipe. I will definitely be making it again.
I have never made pumpkin pie, and this was soo good! I like a lot of spices, I doubled the amount of spices and it was perfect. The texture was amazing and set perfectly

This was the best pumpkin pie I've ever eaten! Taking others' input about the sugar, I only used 3/4 cup and it was plenty sweet, and made my puree from a white pie pumpkin. I halved the recipe to make 1 pie. Everything was easy to split except the eggs, so I used 1 egg and 1 egg white. Delicious!!!

Delicious! I listened to the other reviewers and ended up also using just 1 cup of sugar, which gave the perfect amount of sweetness. I also used oat milk in place of regular milk since that's what I had on hand. Will definitely stick to this recipe next time I'm craving pumpkin pie!
We made this for Thanksgiving and the flavor was incredible!!!
This pie was good, but required a bit of chilling for it to become easy enough to get a clean cut. We loved the flavor, though!
